track.title: Abu-Ata
track.notes: Tagged title: Abu Ata. Same audio as 'Ahmad Ebadi, Setar Solo' (2000), CD1 track 2 (Abu'ata I), sample-aligned; that release is not analysed separately.

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on C5 and dwells most on C in Phrase 1. Phrase 2 (0:10.0) introduces D, centred on C. Phrase 17 (4:19.5) introduces Bk, centred on C. The line peaks at D5 (573.5 Hz) at 0:20.6. It closes on C4, not the tonic (G4 → G4 → G4 → Ak4 → Ak4 → C4).

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes

flags: tonic G set in the catalog (Abu-Ata keeps Shur's finalis (Farhat 1990, p. 35; Zonis 1973, p. 71); in this track's pitch set Shur sits on about G -45 cents (191 Hz). The vote picked the 4th above, Abu-Ata's shahed (Farhat 1990, p. 35). Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 257.9 Hz (C)
